old.group: The bronze, the slipway, the sea-wall
old.name: Archaeological Museum of Piraeus
old.teaser: Four Classical bronzes in one room, pulled from a 1959 sewer
old.text: In July 1959 workmen digging a sewer at Georgiou A' and Filonos struck a bronze hand 1.5 m down; below lay four gods packed in ash with a coin of 87/86 BC — loot crated for Sulla's ships after he stormed Athens in 86 BC. Room 3 holds them now: the Piraeus Apollo, the oldest hollow-cast kouros known, with the Athena and the two Artemis. Sixty to ninety minutes; closed Tuesdays.
old.meta: HOURS Wed–Mon 09:00–17:00 (Apr–Oct) / 08:30–15:30 (Nov–Mar), closed Tue · €10 · 31 Charilaou Trikoupi St, uphill from Zea marina

culture:Zea Shipsheds (ancient neosoikoi.group: The bronze, the slipway, the sea-wall

old.group: The bronze, the slipway, the sea-wall
old.name: Zea Shipsheds (ancient neosoikoi)
old.teaser: Trireme slipways of c. 480 BC, seen through a basement window
old.text: Under the yachts of Pasalimani lie the bones of the fleet that saved Greece. The Zea Harbour Project (Bjørn Lovén, Danish Institute) carbon-dated shipshed timbers to roughly 520–480 BC — stone slipways that likely cradled the triremes rowed to Salamis in 480. Nearly 400 such sheds once ringed Piraeus; three survive, walled into an apartment basement and lit only by what leaks through a ground-floor window. Nothing to enter — you peer in from the street.
old.meta: FREE · viewed from the street, anytime · Akti Moutsopoulou at Sirangiou St, NE corner of the yacht basin (coords approximate)

culture:Hellenic Maritime Museum.group: The bronze, the slipway, the sea-wall

old.group: The bronze, the slipway, the sea-wall
old.name: Hellenic Maritime Museum
old.teaser: A museum built around Konon's 4th-c. BC sea-wall, sub tower on the quay
old.text: When the museum settled at Zea in 1971 it kept the ground it stood on: threading the halls runs a length of the very fortification the port was famous for — the sea-wall Themistocles began after Salamis and Konon rebuilt in the 4th c. BC. Outside on the quay stands the conning tower of the WWII submarine Papanikolis. A museum of ships that is itself a fragment of the wall that once guarded them. No photography inside; mornings only.
old.meta: HOURS Tue–Sat 09:00–14:00, closed Sun/Mon · €5 / €3 reduced · Akti Themistokleous, Marina Zeas

culture:Municipal Theatre of Piraeus.group: The stage, indoors and open to the gulf

old.group: The stage, indoors and open to the gulf
old.name: Municipal Theatre of Piraeus
old.tag: price varies · Korai Sq · by season
old.teaser: An 1895 neoclassical house with a rare surviving wooden stage
old.text: Piraeus architect Ioannis Lazarimos laid the foundation in 1884 and opened the theatre on 9 April 1895 behind a four-column Corinthian portico. It closed for about a decade, then restoration works of 2008–2013 reopened it on 22 October 2013 and uncovered the original 1895 wooden stage, one of few surviving in Europe — red velvet, gilt, a painted ceiling. A working house, not a daytime monument: catch a performance or a scheduled tour, and there is no summer programme here.
old.meta: HOURS autumn–spring season; box office Mon–Sat (not Tue) ~10:00–14:00 & evenings · price varies · Korai Square, 32 Iroon Politechniou Ave — check dithepi.gr

culture:Veakeio Municipal Theatre.group: The stage, indoors and open to the gulf

old.group: The stage, indoors and open to the gulf
old.name: Veakeio Municipal Theatre
old.teaser: 2,000 open-air seats cut into the hill, the Saronic Gulf below
old.text: Two thousand seats cut into Profitis Ilias hill, ~87 m above the sea. Poured in concrete in 1969 under the dictatorship as the 'Skylitseio', opening with Verdi's Nabucco; in 1976 restored democracy renamed it for Emilios Veakis, the Piraeus-born tragedian hounded in the post-war terror — an authoritarian monument turned into a memorial to the actor it had once ignored. Renovated 2024–25, its summer season kept. Summer only, open-air, up a steep hill on hard stone seating.
old.meta: HOURS summer only (Jun–Sep), curtain ~21:00 · price varies; many municipal nights low-cost or free · Profitis Ilias hill, above Mikrolimano

old.name: Municipal Gallery of Piraeus
old.tag: free · old Post Office · weekday mornings
old.teaser: Early-modern Greek painting inside a Neoclassical post office
old.text: Piraeus posted its letters here for decades; now the old Post Office posts its painters instead. Founded 1957 and holding some 837 works, the restored Neoclassical hall gathers the port's artists — chief among them the Corfu-born scenographer Panos Aravantinos (Corfu 1884 – Paris 1930), a celebrated set-designer for the Berlin State Opera whose collection was bequeathed to Piraeus on his death. His stage worlds hang for free beside Georgios Kastriotis sculpture. Short weekday hours; call ahead or find it shut.
old.meta: HOURS Mon–Fri ~10:00–14:00 (confirm weekends by phone) · free · 29 Filonos St, cnr Karaoli Dimitriou

old.name: Cine Melina
old.teaser: An open-air municipal cinema in the 1922 refugee quarter
old.text: Drapetsona grew from the tents of 1922 Asia Minor refugees in the shadow of the Lipasmata fertiliser works — for decades a byword for poisoned air and rebetiko grief. Its summer cinema answers with a low-cost municipal ticket, and free tribute nights, in a courtyard of climbing vines, and carries the name of Melina Mercouri, whose 'Never on Sunday' turned a Piraeus dockside woman into an international figure. The poorest quarter of the port screens its films for a couple of euros. Summer only; mostly Greek programming.
old.meta: HOURS summer only (Jun–Sep), screenings after dark ~21:00 · €3 Mon–Thu / €5 Fri–Sun (two films) / €3 reduced, tributes free · 65 Sokratous St, Drapetsona

old.name: I Anemi (Zacharoula N. Kordoni)
old.teaser: The last working rope-house of Piraeus, cut to the metre
old.text: The anemi is the big rope-twisting reel the shop is named for. In 1936 the Kordoni family spun rope by hand on the first anemes for Greece's busiest port, opened this retail counter in 1970, and by 1990 the third generation had added brass fittings, fenders and life-rings. The surname Kordoni means 'cord'. Three-strand rope still comes off the reel and gets cut to your length across the counter — Greek-first, weekday mornings, nothing decorative to browse.
old.meta: HOURS Mon–Fri 07:00–16:30, Sat 07:00–14:30, closed Sun · rope by the metre (€–€€) · Kapodistriou 29

craft:Banks Sails Greece.group: The other, and what it is missing

old.name: Banks Sails Greece
old.teaser: A working sail loft on the floor above the fishing harbour
old.text: It began in 1987 as Yacht-Care Sailmakers — two champions, Spyros and Dimitris, and a few sewing machines above the fishing harbour. In 2008 the loft joined the Italian Banks Sails network and started dressing boats to 141 feet; in 2020 Spyros' world-ranked twin sons, George and Stratis, took over — sailmakers who race the sails they cut. Also biminis, sprayhoods and stackpacks, with ORCi and IRC certification. Call first: a by-appointment loft, nothing to buy off a shelf.
old.meta: BY APPOINTMENT · made-to-measure sails and canvas (€€€) · Papadiamanti 1, Mikrolimano

craft:No class to enrol in.brief: tag 'honestly', NO place/Maps. The honest warning for the craft section: neither the rope-house nor the sail loft runs a class you can enrol in (verify if either does now); what you can do is buy rope cut to the metre or commission/repair a sail. Say so plainly.

old.name: O Stavros
old.teaser: Briki coffee and fried market smelt inside a market arcade.
old.text: Inside Stoa Kampanidi, hard beside the Municipal Market off Gounari, a kafeneio-ouzeri that has not changed for the men who work the port. Greek coffee comes under a thick skin of kaïmaki, drunk beside fried smelt served on tin, early, among market porters and sailors. LiFO filed it in 2019 among the surviving old kafeneia of the port. Go at first light, and leave the laptop shut — this is a ritual, not a coffee bar.

old.name: O Stamatis
old.teaser: A kafeneio where time stopped in 1935 — ring before you go.
old.text: On Leocharous, in the streets behind the Municipal Market, a kafeneio-ouzeri frozen at 1935 — the framed original operating licence still hangs on the wall, briki coffee brewed at marble among fifty-year regulars. Its last confirmed trace is a 2019 LiFO feature, so this is an if-it's-still-trading pilgrimage: phone 210 4129071 before you cross. Come late morning; the pull is the room, not the coffee technique.
old.meta: HOURS daytime · market hours · PRICE € · phone 210 4129071 first

old.name: Möte
old.teaser: Specialty coffee in a light-flooded 1936 corner room.
old.text: The one café in Piraeus where a World Brewers Cup champion's team — Stefanos Domatiotis, who took that title in 2014 — picks and profiles the single-origin beans. They pour them in a high-ceilinged 1936 corner on Sotiros Dios, big windows facing the light, coffee-first and unhurried. Come weekday mid-morning for a pour-over Ethiopia 'Buki', floral and tea-clear — the one room here quiet enough to open a laptop in.
old.meta: HOURS Mon–Sat 07:30–21:30 · Sun closed · PRICE €€ specialty

old.name: Eighteenscreen Micro Roastery
old.teaser: A from-green micro-roastery you climb the hill for
old.text: Opened 2009 as one of Greece's first specialty micro-roasteries, up the Tzavella slope of Kastella where the neighbourhood still climbs for a filter. Q Grader Giannis Gkiourtzian roasts the bean from green through repeated tastings; the single-origin cup is the reason to leave the flat by the port. A genuine daytime work room, unhurried over a house-roasted filter — not a harbour terrace, no sea view, and it shuts before dark.
old.meta: HOURS ~07:00–17:30 Mon–Fri · until 15:00 Sat · closed Sun · €€ specialty · Tzavella Kitsou 88, Kastella · walk-in

old.name: Oven Roastery
old.teaser: Piraeus's own from-green roaster, opened March 2026
old.text: Dimitris Pantelis apprenticed at Samba, one of Athens' benchmark roasters, then crossed to Piraeus in March 2026 to install a 15kg Loring in a bare concrete-and-wood room at Kastoros 44, a block and a half from the metro terminus. His thesis is sweet coffee: clean green, roasted only to reveal the varietal. Order the Colombian honey pour-over or the fruity Barinas espresso. Small and coffee-first — fine for a short focused sit, not an all-day base; confirm hours, it's brand-new.
old.meta: HOURS daytime (opened March 2026 — confirm) · €€ specialty · Kastoros 44, Agios Dionysios · walk-in

old.name: Belle Amie
old.teaser: An art-deco salon where brunch runs to one in the morning.
old.text: A neoclassical mansion dressed in art deco on the Angelou Metaxa pedestrian street, a step back from Zea. The ground floor was once the Belle Amie ouzeri that Bithikotsis's 1969 hit made famous; now it serves an all-day brunch from nine and keeps pouring cocktails to half-past one, with sea glimpses toward the marina. Come to linger over the room, not to work — a dressed table, not a workspace.
old.meta: HOURS Daily 09:00–01:30 · brunch 09:00–13:00 · PRICE €€–€€€ · book 24h ahead

old.name: East Coast Concept Store
old.teaser: An all-day coffee-and-streetwear concept store, busy and fast
old.text: A Polynesia-inspired all-day concept store since 2020 at Palaiologou 9, inland Terpsithea between the centre and the Piraiki coast. The filter is genuine single-origin specialty — by Area 51 Coffee Roasters — rather than the port's default frappé, but the room runs on brunch, cocktails and its own surf-skate-motorcycle streetwear brand, KVD2137. Come for the cup, the plate and the racks; the service is fast and the crowd steady, so it reads as a lifestyle room, not a quiet desk.
old.meta: HOURS all-day · €€ specialty · Palaiologou 9, Terpsithea · walk-in
